texts.preamble: Hindustan Cocacola Beverages vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 1 February, 2018 The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh Mcrc-391-2017 (Hindustan Cocacola Beverages Vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh) 10 Jabalpur, Dated : 01-02-2018
texts.facts: This petition under section 482 of the Code of Criminal e Procedure has been filed by the petitioner to invoke the extraordinary ad jurisdiction of this Court and to quash the criminal proceeding of Pr Criminal Case No.1907/2010, pending before the Judicial Magistrate First Class, Hoshangabad and to quash order dated 10.12.2010, a hy whereby cognizance under sections 7 & 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act has been taken against the petitioner. The petitioner ad is a Company, namely, Hindustan Coca-Cola Beverages Pvt.Ltd. M through its authorized person-Shri Ratnesh Pandey. 2. The prosecution case, in brief, is that the Food Inspector, of Jagdish Prasad Lawanshi taken a sample on 10.9.2010 from Shiv rt General Stores after introducing himself and observing the necessary ou formalities. The "Thums Up" cold drink of 1.25 Ltrs. was found with the label and the date of manufacturing was not legible, therefore, it C was mis-branded and the quality was suspicious. The Batch Number h was also not clear and the packaging date was not mentioned. He took ig 3 samples. One sample was sent to the Laboratory for analysis. H 3. After having found that the sample is mis-branded and it was sub-standard, the prosecution was launched. Letter was sent to the seller, distributor, manufacturer seeking the details under section 14-A of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act (hereinafter referred to the as "PFA Act"). The "Thums-Up" was being manufactured by Hindustan Coca-Cola Beverages Pvt. Ltd. situated at Industrial Area, Pillukhedi, Tahsil Narsinghgarh, Rajgarh (MP). After following the procedure, complaint was filed for violation of sections 2(ix)(k) and 7(ii) of the PFA Act and Rule 32 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules (hereinafter referred to as the "PFA Rules"). 4. On behalf of the petitioner the present petition has been filed on the ground that packaging was properly made. The date of packaging was not clear, therefore, it is claimed to be mis-branded. But, it could be because of so many reasons viz. obliterate or become faint or not clear, which cannot be termed as "mis-branding". It is also claimed that sample was taken on 10.9.2010. The life of the food article was three months. The complaint was filed on 10.12.2010. Notice was received by the petitioner on 20.12.2010, therefore, the petitioner could not send the sample within time. The date Hindustan Cocacola Beverages vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 March, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134028399/ 1 of sh packaging was not required to be engraved in the bottle. On the paper e label, it was printed. However, after sometime the packaging date ad might have been obliterated. It is further claimed that remedy under Pr section 13(2) of the PFA Act was not available to the petitioner because of the delay in filing the complaint and the fact that allegation a was made with regard to mis-branding is not correct. It is claimed that hy complaint was filed after the self life of the food article was over. ad Therefore, the petitioner could not avail the valuable right under M section 13(2) of the PFA Act.
texts.arguments: 5. Learned counsel for the respondent submitted that of printing was not clear and, therefore, the information/entry made in the label was the subject matter of prosecution. As per requirement of rt the PFA Rules the date of packaging was necessary and important, for ou without the date of packaging it is not possible to make out the expiry C date of the product. Therefore, it is misbranding. 7. In this regard, the case of Indrajeet Walia s/o S.Valia vs. Food Inspector Shri Subhash Khedkar [M.Cr.C. No.993/2012 decided on 18.12.2014 High Court of Madhya Pradesh Bench at Indore] which was later on affirmed by the Supreme Court in Special sh Leave Petition No.802/2015 decided on 24.9.2015. ad On behalf of the petitioner reliance has been placed in the case of Pr Nestle India Limited vs. State of Bihar and others, reported as 2015 Cr.L.J. 803, wherein the High Court of Patna has held that such a printing was not clear.
